clue.text: Pamphlet lacking right sensitivity

indicators.note: lacking says the word before it goes without the letter named next

parts.note: a tract is a short religious or political pamphlet
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A leaflet criticised for being tactless and insensitive.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is delicacy in dealing with people, a careful awareness of how others feel.

clue.text: One caught after leading question

indicators.note: after says the word next to it comes second, behind the part that follows

parts.note: being top is leading
the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is collared just after asking a leading question, like a witness tripped up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the parts in a jumbled order: 'after leading' puts the top part first.
explanation.definitionFit: A question in the sense of a matter under discussion is a subject or theme for debate.

clue.text: Lifting mask, in essence, is damaging

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the word that follows

parts.note: the core of something is its essence

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something makes it read from the bottom up

parts.note: a visor is a mask or face guard

explanation.surface: Removing one's mask is, at heart, a harmful act.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrosive means wearing away or destructive, so it describes something damaging.

clue.text: Pro, present before noon, excused

parts.note: to be pro something is to be for it
to present is to give
N is an abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A professional who shows up before midday is let off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being forgiven means being pardoned for a fault, so excused fits.

clue.text: Idea from sleuth, breaking bulb

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: an onion is a bulb vegetable
PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A detective has a bright idea, as if a light bulb has gone on.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief someone holds, close to an idea.

clue.text: Favourable record written up before retreat

indicators.note: in a down clue anything written up reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a log is a written record
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A good report filed before someone withdraws.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden opportunity is a very favourable or advantageous one.

clue.text: Summarise, in change of tune, vital funding for new business

indicators.note: in puts the first word inside the rearranged letters
a change of the words that follow means their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, as fodder
to recap is to summarise

explanation.surface: Summarising a music change, before mentioning vital money for a start-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vital' looks like part of the definition, but it joins 'tune' as the letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture capital is money invested in new, risky enterprises by backers seeking returns.

clue.text: Famous piece of music with depth

parts.note: a single note is a small piece of music
D is an abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A celebrated composition with real profundity.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or celebrated, the same as famous.

clue.text: Strange place occupied by nuns in alliance with Capone?

indicators.note: the nuns' place sits in the word for an alliance

parts.note: a union is an alliance
a convent is the house where nuns live
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: An odd scene: nuns joining forces with Al Capone.
explanation.walkthrough: The image of nuns allied with a gangster is deliberately bizarre, which suits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional means departing from the norm, which is what strange or odd describes.

clue.text: Endanger number, supporting spoliation of earth

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting part sits underneath, so it comes last
spoliation is plundering and ruining, so the word after it is wrecked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Plundering the planet puts a great many at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten something is to put it in danger, so it matches endanger.

clue.text: Enduring ring receiving private backing

indicators.note: the ring takes something in, holding it inside

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

indicators.note: backing a word means running it in the opposite direction

parts.note: inner means private, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: A marriage band that keeps lasting because of a backer's confidential support.
explanation.definitionFit: Perennial means lasting through the years, constantly recurring, which is enduring.

clue.text: Drama about time beginning for convict in nick

indicators.note: about means going around something else

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A prison play about a criminal starting his sentence in the nick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for prison, which steers the surface, but the definition is the other sense: a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, the same as a nick in an edge.

clue.text: Film in city following line of people

indicators.note: following puts the word before it second, behind the phrase after it

parts.note: a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs
Dundee is a Scottish city

explanation.surface: A movie set in a town where people queue in line.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a crocodile is a long file of schoolchildren walking two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodile Dundee is the 1986 Australian comedy starring Paul Hogan, a well-known movie.

clue.text: French wine consumed by composer feeling sorrow

indicators.note: something consumed by another is taken inside it

parts.note: Edvard Grieg, the Norwegian composer
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A melancholy composer drowns his sorrows in claret.
explanation.definitionFit: Grieving means mourning or suffering deep sadness, which is feeling sorrow.

clue.text: Measure of power mostly absent in performance, dry

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a gig is a live performance
away means absent
TT means teetotal, so dry

explanation.surface: An unplugged, alcohol-free concert where the power is largely missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigawatt is a unit of power equal to a billion watts.

clue.text: Allow appeal after wave

indicators.note: after puts the word before it second, behind the word that follows

parts.note: a perm is a permanent wave in the hair
it means sex appeal, as in having it

explanation.surface: Granting an appeal once a wave has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to give permission, to let something happen.

clue.text: Spymaster with cruel air, terribly volatile

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

indicators.note: terribly means badly done, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A spy chief with a cruel manner is dangerously unpredictable.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercurial describes someone with sudden changes of mood, which makes them volatile.

clue.text: Environmentalists in meagre ensemble

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters sit across the two words

explanation.surface: A small band of eco-campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greens are members of Green parties, political environmentalists.

clue.text: Resistance during ritual shaken by new test

indicators.note: during places one thing inside another
shaken letters are jumbled into another order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
N is an abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A rehearsal ceremony disrupted by protesters and something novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a practice rehearsal to see how something works, a test.

clue.text: Satisfied agent with tons in shelter

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent

indicators.note: in puts the tons inside the word for shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: An agent is content with plenty of goods stored under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means full, especially after eating, so satisfied.

clue.text: Disregard good number seized by rage

indicators.note: something seized by another is held within it

parts.note: ire is anger
G is an abbreviation for good
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Overlooking a fine song taken over by an angry outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay no attention to it, which is to disregard it.

clue.text: Wife pounds clothing in huge pails, badly short of energy and detergent

indicators.note: clothing wraps around what follows, so it goes inside
badly arranged letters are put in the wrong order
short of means lacking, so the letter named next is removed

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written, as fodder
E is the symbol for energy
quid is slang for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A wife sloshing laundry in great buckets, but running out of energy and soap.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife and the money together wrap round the jumbled letters. Washing-up liquid is the British name for dish soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing-up liquid is the soap used for dishes, a kind of detergent.

clue.text: Search, getting bad-tempered, catching cold

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside

parts.note: a sour person is bad-tempered
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone hunting about grows grumpy after catching a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: scouring a place means combing through every corner thoroughly while looking for something.

clue.text: Material dug up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: mined means dug, as for coal

explanation.surface: Stuff excavated from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill fabric, a type of material.

clue.text: Projection? Hard to cut rent

indicators.note: to cut something is to go into it, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: rent as a past participle means torn
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Is a forecast that rent will be hard to reduce?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; here it is the past tense of rend, meaning ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp point sticking out from a stem, a small projection.

clue.text: Clear about proportion in campaign

indicators.note: about means going around something

parts.note: open means clear or unobstructed
a ratio is a proportion

explanation.surface: Getting things in proportion within a military push.
explanation.definitionFit: A military operation is an organised series of actions, a campaign.

clue.text: Thankful to take cover, lying back in grass

indicators.note: in places the cover word inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: a word lying back is laid out in the opposite direction

parts.note: a veil is a cover

explanation.surface: A soldier glad to hide, stretched out in the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling relieved means being freed from worry, so grateful or thankful.

clue.text: Feather mostly purple

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a plume is a feather

explanation.surface: A quill largely dyed violet.
explanation.definitionFit: Plum is a deep reddish-purple colour named after the fruit.
